transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-10-06 16:00 PT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Tariq Soto (Head of Integrations - Sentinel Syndicate), Lena Morales (Eng Manager), Priya Desai (Security & Compliance), Evan K. (Product), Marco Lin (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Quick sync on packaging and checklist for marketplace listing; technical blockers around KMS and air-gapped images; agreed to run a short perf window and share helm chart + packaging docs.

---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick rollcall?
[00:05] Tariq (Sentinel): Hey, Tariq here.
[00:07] Lena: Lena here.
[00:09] Priya: Priya on the line.
[00:11] Evan: Evan.
[00:13] Marco: Marco, SRE.
[00:15] Jordan (Redwood): Jordan here, thanks. Maya: you wanna kick off?
[00:18] Maya: Yep, thanks. So agenda — packaging for marketplace listing, VPC/KMS compatibility for private deployment, and perf/benchmark plan. We'll run down a checklist then dive into the Helm and image requirements.
[00:31] Tariq: Sounds good. The main constraint for us is that our internal marketplace needs an on-prem/hybrid connector that can be deployed behind our customers' firewalls,
[00:39] Lena: and we also need the images to be reproducible, signed, and able to be pulled from an internal registry.
[00:43] Marco: We run air-gapped clusters for GOV customers, so images often need to be pre-pulled or provided as tarballs.
[00:48] Jordan: Got it. That's in line with other partners. We'll go over our helm packaging and also an alternative operator flow if you prefer an image tarball path.
[00:56] Maya: Before we get deep, quick qual: are you planning to list the connector in your marketplace (public) or use it as a private listing for enterprise customers?
[01:05] Tariq: Private listing first, likely. Public later but that's months out.
[01:09] Maya: Ok good. That helps with some requirements — we'll focus on private-listing controls.
[01:13]
[01:30] Jordan: From a runtime point: Redwood's private deployment supports a Helm chart we maintain plus an optional operator that handles upgrades and key rotation. The important pieces for you are: KMS integration (we support external KMS via env var mapping or a KMS adapter), image signing verification, and a lightweight sidecar for telemetry if you want token-level metering.
[01:50] Priya: For security, our auditors need to see KMS key import/export controls and evidence of envelope encryption. Also SSO and RBAC for the management console.
[01:58] Jordan: We can provide KMS integration docs — we support Amazon KMS, Azure Key Vault, and our KMS adapter for self-managed HSMs. The adapter runs as a small container and proxies calls, so in air-gapped envs you can run it alongside.
[02:14] Lena: Is the adapter open-source? We need to review license.
[02:17] Jordan: Yes, the adapter repo is MIT-licensed. I'll paste links in the follow-up.
[02:22]
[02:35] Evan: From product: we want to confirm pricing hooks — how will we meter usage so it shows up in our billing dashboard?
[02:42] Maya: Good question. We provide a metering shim that emits usage events to a configurable endpoint (webhook) or writes to local logs for offline ingestion. For private listings the usual pattern is to forward usage to your metering collector, which can then consolidate with your billing.
[02:57] Marco: How real-time are those events? We need near-real-time for some customers.
[03:02] Jordan: Typically events are emitted < 30s, but depends on batching settings. We can tune for lower latency at cost of higher network traffic. That's where the latency vs cost tradeoff shows up.
[03:12]
[03:25] Priya: Also we need attestation for image signing — does Redwood enforce signed images or is it optional?
[03:30] Jordan: Optional by default, but for marketplace listing we recommend requiring signed images. The Helm chart has an admission-hook flag to reject unsigned images. We can set that in the sample values.yaml.
[03:42] Lena: Perfect. We also run a policy engine (OPA) — can we inject an OPA check?
[03:47] Jordan: Yes, we have a policy plugin interface. The helm chart exposes a sidecar extension point where you can add OPA and register the policy path. We'll document the hooks.
[03:56] Maya: Great. Let's pivot to packaging specifics — Jordan, can you screen-share the high-level layout or walk through the files? (Note: recording shows they referenced a deck: https://redwood.example.com/partners/sentinel-packaging-deck)
[04:10] Jordan: Sure. The helm chart is under charts/redwood-connector, top-level has Chart.yaml, values.yaml, templates/. The values.yaml has sections: image.pullPolicy, image.signature.required, kms.adapter.enabled, telemetry.sidecar.enabled, marketplace.metadata. We also include a packaging script that emits a tarball with provenance and signed digest.
[04:35] Tariq: Is the packaging script runnable without internet?
[04:38] Jordan: Yes, we added an offline mode where it reads local image tarballs and populates the manifest. You do need openssl for signing unless you provide a signing binary yourself.
[04:46] Marco: Can you produce an OCI layout tarball for our air-gapped flow?
[04:49] Jordan: Yep, we can output OCI layout and accompanying SBOM.
[04:54]
[05:10] Lena: About the marketplace metadata — what fields do you require for private listing?
[05:15] Maya: Required: name, version, semantic versioning, publisher info, short description, minimum supported runtime (e.g., K8s >= 1.24), recommended instance profiles (gpus/cpu/ram), and a declared "connectivity mode" (internet, proxy, or air-gapped). Optional: early-access notes, known limitations, and benchmark numbers.
[05:36] Evan: Benchmarks — can you share suggested test harness? We wanna show tokens/sec and p95 latency for default prompt mixes.
[05:44] Jordan: We'll share a perf script that runs the same prompt sets we use in Redwood Optimize: short, medium, long tokens, and measures throughput and p95. We'll include load profile and a simple harness based on curl + KV cache warmup.
[05:59] Marco: For SRE, how do we manage KV cache persistence across restarts? We prefer persistent volumes.
[06:05] Jordan: The chart supports PV-backed KV cache (Redis or local RocksDB with PVC). For high-scale we recommend Redis with persistence to disk.
[06:15]
[06:30] Priya: A couple of redlines from security: 1) KMS audit ledger; 2) TLS mutual auth for internal control plane; 3) SSO with SAML. Can you confirm those?
[06:40] Jordan: Yes on all three. KMS audit ledger: the adapter can forward audit logs to your logging cluster; TLS mTLS is supported on the admin ports; SAML SSO is supported via the management console — we'll include configuration snippets.
[06:53] Priya: And where are logs stored by default? We need retention policies.
[06:57] Jordan: By default logs are stdout to the container and rely on your cluster-level logging; the chart can be configured to send structured JSON logs to a local sidecar or forwarder. Retention is by your infra.
[07:07]
[07:30] Maya: Quick note — for marketplace listing approval you'll need our compliance pack (SOC2 extract, GDPR notes). I'll attach that.
[07:36] Priya: Please do. We only need excerpts, not full reports.
[07:40] Maya: Will do.
[07:42]
[07:55] Jordan: Now, small snag we sometimes hit: GPU driver versions and specific CUDA toolkits can change perf characteristics. For the sample size profiles we include recommended CUDA versions and a small compatibility matrix.
[08:08] Marco: We have mixed clusters — some nodes are A100, some T4. Does the helm chart support node selectors or device plugin annotations?
[08:15] Jordan: Yep, values.yaml exposes nodeSelector, tolerations, and devicePlugin args. We also have a runtime classifier that can pick a compatible kernel path for T4 vs A100. It's automatic in the image but tunable.
[08:29] Lena: Ok. For initial pilot, our plan is to run 3x small instances in staging and push about 100 concurrent short requests to simulate traffic.
[08:37] Jordan: That's reasonable for a sanity test. For representative perf numbers, we recommend a mix with 10% long context requests to validate KV cache effectiveness.
[08:47]
[09:05] Evan: On the billing side, if we consume Redwood licenses for the underlying model, do we bill per token or per-instance?
[09:12] Maya: For private deployments the usual model is a hybrid: licensing fee per-instance plus per-token metering optionally. We can align to your billing model — the metering shim emits token counts you can ingest.
[09:24] Tariq: Do you have sample invoices or pricing ranges to share?
[09:28] Maya: We'll send a templated pricing sheet; it's not final but will help your procurement.
[09:34]
[09:50] Jordan: Quick tech deep: our runtime supports continuous batching and a KV cache that reduces repeated context cost. For your workload patterns (you mentioned a lot of repeated prompts in the product), the cache will reduce tokens/sec by up to 30% in our measurements.
[10:06] Marco: What's the memory profile for a single KV shard?
[10:10] Jordan: Depends on kv entries; rough rule: 1GB per million tokens cached for compressed representation, but we'll provide a calculator.
[10:19]
[10:30] Priya: Anything about exportable audit logs for compliance?
[10:33] Jordan: We can produce exportable logs with redaction options. There's also a low-level hook for you to forward to Splunk/ELK.
[10:41]
[11:05] Maya: Okay turning to the canary/rollout plan — Jordan, what's your recommended canary for a private listing?
[11:12] Jordan: Start with 2 nodes in staging, then 5% of traffic in pilot, monitor p95 and error rate for a day, then 25% roll for 24-48 hours. Use automatic rollback if p95 increases by >25% or errors over threshold.
[11:28] Lena: Do you expose tracing? We want distributed traces to tie requests back to customer requests.
[11:33] Jordan: Yes, we support OpenTelemetry traces and can forward to your collector.
[11:38] Evan: Good.
[11:42]
[12:05] Marco: One operational note — image registry auth. We sometimes rotate registry creds frequently. Does the chart support imagePullSecrets refresh without redeploy?
[12:12] Jordan: The operator can rotate secrets if you integrate with your secret manager; otherwise you do a rolling restart. We can provide an example CRD for secrets rotation.
[12:22]
[12:40] Priya: Do you have a recommended retention period for KV cache? Some of our customers have strict data retention windows.
[12:46] Jordan: The cache TTL is configurable per namespace; you can set it to 0 for no persistence or implement evictions. We'll include examples in values.
[12:57] Maya: Quick check: timeline? When do you want the staging perf run?
[13:02] Tariq: Week of 10/18 is good. We'll need the helm and sample scripts before then.
[13:07] Maya: We'll target sending the artifacts by 10/13.
[13:11]
[13:25] Jordan: Any questions about marketplace metadata fields or the packaging outputs?
[13:30] Lena: One more — licensing header in the chart. We need a clear statement around support windows and EOL.
[13:36] Maya: We'll include an explicit support and EOL section in the listing metadata.
[13:40]
[13:55] Evan: Competitor callouts — we evaluated CloudAI last quarter; they required a heavier agent and had limited offline packaging. How is Redwood different here?
[14:04] Maya: Our focus was to keep the connector lightweight and to support offline packaging and OCI layout outputs. EdgeServe pushed an operator-first model which couples too tightly to their control plane; ours can be run fully offline.
[14:17] Evan: Good to know.
[14:20]
[14:35] Jordan: Ok, I'll summarize the artifacts we'll send: 1) helm chart and sample values.yaml, 2) offline packaging script and OCI tarball example, 3) perf harness and scripts, 4) KMS adapter docs and sample config, 5) compliance/ SOC2 excerpts, 6) marketplace metadata template.
[14:58] Tariq: Excellent. For the perf harness, can we run a short 2-hour window and capture traces?
[15:04] Jordan: Yes — invite our SE account and we'll coordinate.
[15:08] Marco: We'll make staging accessible and provide a KMS test key.
[15:12]
[15:25] Priya: A security note — for the KMS adapter in airgap, who holds the signing keys? We want to ensure key custody is with us.
[15:33] Jordan: Key custody remains with you. The adapter simply proxies. We'll not have private keys.
[15:38] Priya: Ok, need that in writing.
[15:40] Maya: We'll include a statement in the compliance pack.
[15:44]
[15:55] Lena: Are there known limitations around quantization that affect output quality? Some models drop coherence when quantized heavily.
[16:02] Jordan: Yes — heavy quantization can reduce quality. We provide quantization profiles with recommended settings for different model families; for production-grade output we recommend the middle-tier quantization that preserves fp16-equivalent quality. We'll include our evaluation notes.
[16:20] Evan: Any specifics on memory savings numbers?
[16:24] Jordan: Roughly 2x-4x depending on profile, but it depends on sequence length. We'll send a small table.
[16:31]
[16:45] Maya: A quick recap of decisions and owners:
[16:49] Maya: Redwood to send helm chart, packaging script, perf harness, compliance excerpts by 2027-10-13.
[16:56] Maya: Sentinel to provision staging and KMS test key and run perf window week of 2027-10-18.
[17:02] Maya: We'll plan a follow-up call to review perf results on 2027-10-20 — does that work?
[17:07] Tariq: Yes that works.
[17:09] Lena: Works for me.
[17:11]
[17:28] Jordan: Quick note — we'll include a sample Grafana dashboard and alert thresholds for p95 and error rates in the artifacts.
[17:35] Marco: Useful.
[17:38]
[17:50] Priya: One last compliance ask — we need to ensure the telemetry sidecar can be disabled entirely if customers don't want any data leaving cluster.
[17:58] Jordan: Yes, telemetry is opt-in and can be disabled at chart install. We'll document default-off settings.
[18:06]
[18:25] Maya: Alright, thanks everyone. We'll distribute artifacts and follow-up with calendar invite for the perf review. Any final items?
[18:33] Evan: None from product.
[18:35] Lena: All set.
[18:37] Tariq: Thanks all.
[18:39] Priya: Thanks.
[18:41] Maya: Thanks, talk soon.
